#Comparing the prior season's win percentage with the change in price. 


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/katefisher12/JOUR-405/main/project/"

# Names match the 29 columns in each team-record CSV, in order.
column_names <- c(
  "year", "league", "reported_team",
  "wins", "losses", "ties",
  "division_finish", "playoff_result",
  "points_for", "points_against", "point_difference",
  "coaches", "av_leader", "passing_leader",
  "rushing_leader", "receiving_leader",
  "offense_points_rank", "offense_yards_rank",
  "defense_points_rank", "defense_yards_rank",
  "turnover_rank", "points_differential_rank",
  "yards_differential_rank", "league_teams",
  "margin_of_victory", "strength_of_schedule",
  "srs", "offensive_srs", "defensive_srs"
)

# These columns should remain text.
text_columns <- c(
  "league", "reported_team", "division_finish",
  "playoff_result", "coaches", "av_leader",
  "passing_leader", "rushing_leader", "receiving_leader"
)

read_team <- function(filename, team_name) {
  read_csv(
    paste0(base_url, filename),
    skip = 2,
    col_names = column_names,
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
  ) |>
    # Keep season rows, excluding any repeated headers.
    filter(str_detect(year, "^[0-9]{4}$")) |>
    mutate(
      across(-all_of(text_columns), parse_double),
      year = as.integer(year),

      # Remove playoff asterisks from the original team names.
      reported_team = str_remove_all(reported_team, fixed("*")),

      # Consistent franchise name, including Washington's older names.
      team = team_name,

      games = wins + losses + ties,
      win_pct = (wins + 0.5 * ties) / games
    ) |>
    relocate(team, year) |>
    arrange(year)
}

cowboys <- read_team("cowboys.csv", "Dallas Cowboys")
eagles <- read_team("eaglesscore.csv", "Philadelphia Eagles")
giants <- read_team("giantsscore.csv", "New York Giants")
commanders <- read_team("commanders.score.csv", "Washington Commanders")

team_records <- bind_rows(cowboys, eagles, giants, commanders)

# Examine the cleaned data.
glimpse(team_records)

team_records |>
  select(team, year, wins, losses, ties, win_pct) |>
  arrange(team, desc(year))
```

#Just looking at win_pct it looks like for the Commanders their highest win percentage was 1940, Cowboys was 1977, Eagles was 1949, Giants was 1929. 

```{r}
mean(team_records$win_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
median(team_records$win_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(team_records$win_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# A mean of 0.517 across all team records is telling me that the average winning percentage is about 51.7%. I would expect that a league wide average would be about 50% because every win is a loss for another team. Which means that these specific teams in the NFL East won a little more than they lost or there are outliers in my data that are not accurate. The median on the other hand is exactly .5 which is expected. The gap between mean and median is very small so I would expect the distribution to be pretty symmetric. The Standard Deviation is 0.197. Taking the mean of 0.5 and subtracting/adding 0.197 from it we can expect most team records to fall between 0.303 and 0.697 whichis a pretty wide spread.
